fact: The MFDP, LRA and CBL joint press conference says the LRA deployed ASYCUDA at major customs and border locations to automate customs processing and reduce manual interventions.
The joint press conference says the LRA upgraded ASYCUDA to Version 4.4 to enable direct electronic integration with commercial banks and the Central Bank of Liberia.
Deputy Commerce Minister Wilmot A. Reeves said an upgrade of ASYCUDA World is among reforms under the Liberia Investment, Finance and Trade Project.
The LRA Corporate Strategic Plan 2025-2029 says ASYCUDA has played a pivotal role in augmenting customs operations and tables its status as extended to Freeport of Liberia, RIA and Buchanan.
The plan tables an ASYCUDA extension project with expected result of extension to five rural ports.
LRA Commissioner General James Dorbor Jallah said ASYCUDA has been deployed to 11 of 17 Customs Business Offices.
Jallah said ASYCUDA is deployed to 11 of 17 Customs Business Offices, with solar power and connectivity being introduced at rollout locations outside Monrovia.

The Ministry of Commerce and Industry issued an open international tender on 9 June 2026, World Bank-financed, for supply of ICT infrastructure (servers, storage, networking, training) for the National Single Window System for the Liberia Revenue Authority, shared with MOA, MOCI and LISA.

ECOWAS says it launched deployment of SIGMAT between Cote d'Ivoire, Guinea and Liberia in Monrovia on 31 October 2025, exchanging electronic transit messages through interconnection of their national customs systems.

Liberia's report to the WTO Trade Facilitation Agreement database says that under the World Bank-funded LIFT-P, led by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, a National Single Window is being built through UNCTAD's ASYCUDA Programme, with the current phase integrating three government agencies and ASYCUDA to be upgraded.

The Liberia Revenue Authority says on 3 November 2025 that importers and agents in Liberia can now submit declarations electronically through the SIGMAT portal, and that its ASYCUDA team supervises the national customs system.

The Liberia Revenue Authority says ECOWAS launched SIGMAT in Monrovia in late October 2025, a customs data exchange system connecting national customs systems of ECOWAS members, with Liberia, Cote d'Ivoire and Guinea forming the latest corridor.
The Liberia Revenue Authority says ASYCUDA World is live at six customs offices including Roberts International Airport, Buchanan Port and Bo Waterside, with Toe Town and Harper to follow.
